text:
Edmonton's record says contender: 17-5-3, 37 points, a 98% playoff chance by our numbers. The play says something more uncomfortable. The Oilers have 49% of the expected goals (the quality of the chances) and 46% at five on five, and they have scored 25 more goals than their chances usually produce. Our numbers credit them with about ten points of luck. Saturday's 7-4 loss in Carolina, outshot 36-15, was what the underlying numbers look like when the finishing doesn't bail them out.

The finishing is mostly Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl, which is a reasonable thing to build a season around. The headlines have been about McDavid chasing Wayne Gretzky's records, with Gretzky himself saying he wants to see them broken, and about Mike Babcock splitting McDavid and Draisaitl. Together they are still the best line in the building: 22 goals for, 8 against, 60% of the chances. The problem is everyone else. The Joseph, Formenton and Michaels line sits at 31% of the chances, and the Murphy and Shea pair at 42%. Evan Bouchard has become the early Norris pick in several trophy trackers.

In net, Devon Levi set an Oilers record with 10 wins in 11 games before Saturday's seven-goal afternoon, and Tristan Jarry is at .951 over his last five starts. What to watch is depth: whether Babcock finds a second line that can hold its own.
